J A Costello wrote The Siwash, a book of Native life and lore on Puget Sound. The Calvert Company issued it in Seattle in eighteen hundred ninety five. Costello and Samuel F Coombs held its rights that year. Vancouver’s ship Discovery, of seventeen hundred ninety two, fronts the book.

Forty two short chapters range the whole Northwest coast in turn. A bit of history and the fifty four forty cry start it. Flathead and Chinook folk get their own close chapters. The Chinook trade tongue earns a study of its own here. Old-Man-House and Skokomish tribes take long, fond turns. Great spirits, thunderbirds, and the first frog fill the myths. Sealth and the Makah close the roll of tribes in the book. Potlatch feasts and hop field work show life as Costello saw it.
